description: Plan step R4b (graph node rules). Queueing: waiting tickets, wake-up messages, hand-over to the dispatch root, expiry, /rules let and /rules cancel, the per-step reminder, the heartbeat file writer, the queue/block denial texts. DSH runtime row touched: probe required. Depends on FEAT-006.
steps: Read rules design sec 6.3 (everything except the stop-level paragraphs, which are FEAT-008), sec 6.4 (queue text, wake texts, the reminder), sec 6.5, sec 5.4 heartbeat file layout (runner is always false here; the election is blocked with detectors), sec 15 R4 ticket cases. Read src/shared/step-notice.ts and how other rows use installStepNotice; read reference/dsh-desktop-0.2.1-rc.3 agent-loop (steer/inject/followup around lines 790-814), dsh-goal (goals.get / GoalError), dsh-session (session/disposed, origin 'subagent') in the MAIN checkout's reference/ before coding.

Specs first (new tests/rules-tickets.spec.ts; extend tests/rules-row.spec.ts and tests/fake-rc3.ts so the fake host provides what rc.3 provides: calls with parent, live-agent steer/inject/followup recording messages, goals.get with phase and GoalError for a released agent, session/disposed, agents.get): queue verdict opens a ticket and the denial carries its number; same session and same signature reuse the ticket; at most 20 open tickets per session, then block with the 'too many open tickets' text; a nested (parent) call opens a ticket with nested: true using the nested text, and the same-signature direct call reuses it, wake text then says 'from a run_code program'; condition ends -> ticket cleared within the 5 s pass and the original agent gets one message (source hourness-rules-wake) chosen by state: running -> steer; idle with an active goal -> inject; otherwise followup; GoalError from goals.get -> treated as no goal -> followup; a subagent's session ends (both with session/disposed and with only agents.get returning nothing) -> its ticket is handed to the dispatch root (parentSession chain until a session without origin), handedFrom recorded, the root receives the hand-over wake text, a new subagent under the root making the same call reuses the ticket, no live root -> cancelled with the reason written; a person-opened session ending cancels its tickets; expiry: 24 h age, 30 min not retried after cleared, host heartbeat missing or older than 45 s -> expired with expiredWhy, decided in the planning step and not re-derived on replay; a host that is alive but whose heartbeat went stale sends one wake for its host-gone tickets (once per ticket in this process) and degrades health once; /rules let <ticket> lets the next same-signature call through within 10 minutes and closes the ticket, /rules cancel closes it; both refuse for non-human identities; per-step reminder lists only inform rules and the agent's tickets, only when they changed, again after compaction, and in goal rounds; block and queue rules never appear in it; the default rule never appears in it; the heartbeat file has session ids, computed.glmPeak (value or unreadable), catalog state/toldState by each row's activation() or absent, is deleted when no live session for 60 s, old heartbeats (> 1 h) are removed, EPERM on rename retries with backoff and warns once.

Implement src/rules/tickets.ts (open/dedupe/reconcile/handover/expire/wake), src/rules/reminder.ts (step notice through installStepNotice), heartbeat writer in src/rules/heartbeat.ts, wiring in src/rules/index.ts and gate.ts (queue branch; the signature is the first 12 hex digits of SHA-256 of native tool name plus normalised arguments), denial texts per sec 6.4. All host calls (steer, inject, followup, goals.get) wrapped so a throw degrades row health and never escapes the listener or the timer.

Probe scenarios: add rules-handover (a one-off subagent through scripts/probe/probe-dispatch.mjs makes a queued call, hands back and its session ends; after the rule is lifted with /rules (called through the real command handler as the human) the main agent gets the hand-over wake) and a queue scenario: a project rule 'queue calls containing rules-probe-queued while glm-peak is true' under the probe clock (scripts/probe/probe-clock.mjs) and a /rules cancel or condition change, verifying the original session receives the wake message and the retry executes. Also: scenario-end user-level directory has no rules/ folder; request contains the rules reminder exactly when something changed.

Docs in the same commit: ORCHESTRATION.md section 16 (tickets, wake, reminder), DESIGN.md row/degradation tables. Commit at most twice (tickets+reminder; probe+docs). Messages carry gate results including the probe exit code.
acceptance_criteria: A queued call is denied once, the ticket is shared by retries and by a new subagent under the same root, and the original agent is woken exactly once when the condition ends.
Hand-over to the dispatch root works for both disposal signals; a missing root cancels with a written reason.
No host call can throw out of the gate, a timer or an event listener; failures degrade row health with the reason.

Design points interpreted rather than followed (all in ORCHESTRATION.md 16.12):
1. Queue is carried out for the person's rules only; entries of the code (peak levels) stay inert (call runs, nothing journaled). A call hit by both gets a ticket for the person's rules only.
2. A new subagent takes over only a ticket that sits with the dispatch root, is deferred and has handedFrom; the design's wording (any open same-signature ticket under the root) would take a live sibling's ticket away.
3. Tickets of other hosts are never reused or counted for the 20 cap (a dead host's ticket is expired by the next write).
4. A cleared ticket whose agent comes back while the rule holds again: the old ticket is closed done and the call opens a new one. A ticket whose call is now blocked by a stronger rule is cleared (reason 'rule r-x blocks the call now'), not kept.
5. Labels (agentLabel, handedFrom.agentLabel, 'Subagent "<label>"'): the session id, last 8 characters when longer than 12 (a UUID, or session-<uuid>); the design's task label and 'dispatchRoot / focusOf' of M3 do not exist, so the hand-over text has no '(task ...)' part and handedFrom has no focus.
6. The re-judgement also runs right after each /rules command (design: 'when the state file changes'); the 5-second timer covers other hosts' changes. RulesConfig.timer is the test seam.
7. Reminder: the heading line appears only when an inform rule is listed; MAX_ITEMS 12 counts rule lines and the tickets line (the tickets line keeps its place, the rules are cut and counted in 'and N more: call rules_show'); an empty reminder is said once after a non-empty one ('No rules board item applies to you now.').
8. A cleared ticket whose subagent ended is handed over and the root is told at once (hand-over text), since the subagent that got the first wake never ran the call.
9. A host without an agents service (or one whose get throws) hands over nothing, wakes nobody, cancels nothing: tickets stay, health degrades with the reason; person-session cancel on session/disposed needs no registry.
10. The journal reason of a hand-over / cancel on session end says whether the end was seen by the event or by the registry (V11 evidence).
11. Not done: the 'M tickets waiting' clause of the health head (design 11.3), emitMetric calls for ticket events (the receiver does not exist), checking unreadable heartbeat files in the 1-hour sweep (only parseable ones are removed), the L3 check of inject (V3).

Test changes outside the new spec: tests/rules-row.spec.ts 'looking wrote nothing' now expects the host's heartbeat folder and nothing else in .llm/rules/; tests/rules-gate.spec.ts's inert queue test became two (a queue rule defers; entries of the code stay inert); probe checks 'no reminder from the board yet' of glm-rules and non-glm-rules now expect the one reminder of the inform rule in every request.

Verification answers: V11 (a one-off subagent's session emits session/disposed after it hands back): yes in the real runtime (rules-handover; the hand-over record's reason says the session-end event found it). V3 (inject on an idle agent with an active goal): not exercised by any L3 scenario, only against the fake host; FEAT-008's rules-peak-stop probe is the place. Wake method seen in L3: steer (the agent runs a step when the person's command lifts the rule); followup/inject only in the unit specs.

Risks for the reviewer: (a) a wake goes to the agent the registry has; if rc.3 keeps a finished subagent in the registry, a followup could reopen it (not observed: the finished subagent's session was disposed first); (b) tickets are not re-judged after a host restart (they expire host-gone, as designed for ordinary tickets); (c) docs/graph was not touched, so the graph node rules has no record of these commits: the caller records them.
